triage.title: Headline retainer
triage.detail: `cafesat.sat.Vector` (a class group) retains 4.2 MB (14.1% of reachable heap).

triage.title: Concentration
triage.detail: diffuse — retention is spread across multiple roots, so there is no single object to free.

triage.title: Shape
triage.detail: deep (retention flows through long dominator chains — often nested collections or linked structures) — 90% of objects within depth 6, max depth 16.

triage.title: One leak or many
triage.detail: the single biggest object, `java.net.URLClassLoader` (held by `java.lang.Module#loader`), retains 8.8% and the top 10 retain 13.1% of the heap; 1 object(s) each hold >=1%.

triage.title: Classloader reload (low count)
triage.detail: `scala.collection.immutable.$colon$colon` is loaded by 2 class loaders (3.4 MB retained) — possible reload, but count is low; investigate only if count grows.

triage.title: Off-heap (DirectByteBuffer)
triage.detail: 134.3 MB of native memory is held by live DirectByteBuffers — not counted in heap size but can dominate RSS.

triage.title: Sparse object arrays
triage.detail: 38,119 object arrays are <=20% full (5.9 MB wasted on null slots) — sparse or multi-dimensional array structures consuming excess memory.

triage.title: Fixed per-object header overhead
triage.detail: 952,666 objects × 12 B header = 10.9 MB (36.6% of heap) is consumed by JVM object headers alone — consider value types, primitive arrays, or fewer wrapper objects.
